title: Carolingian Empire and the coronation of Charlemagne
summary: On Christmas Day 800, Pope Leo III crowned Charlemagne emperor in Rome. King of the Franks from 768, Charlemagne had extended his rule across modern France, northern Spain, northern Italy and Germany, and sent out commissioners from his capital at Aachen to enforce his decrees. After his death in 814 the empire passed to his son Louis I, and Louis's sons fought for supremacy until the Treaty of Verdun divided it in 843.

uncertainty.note: Charlemagne ruled as King of the Franks from 768 before his imperial coronation on Christmas Day 800; the unified empire was partitioned by the Treaty of Verdun in 843, and the wider Carolingian imperial title collapsed by 888.
